Iteration 2 delivers indoor room-to-room navigation for Nedderman Hall and the Engineering Research Building, one route system shared by every tab, and saved settings, all deployed as a mobile website built with Expo \[1\], React Native \[2\] and React Native for Web \[3\]. This deliverable aims to share the main planning and details about the project without going into too much technical detail. For a more thorough breakdown that could not be covered here, reference the project’s [README.md](https://github.com/AntoVu/cse3311-fall26-group7/blob/main/README.md).

## Changes Since Iteration 1

Many of our starting ideas were changed drastically this iteration, which were appropriately addressed and workarounds/alternatives were found.

### iOS Development Fee

One of the most major and notable points is that Mavigator is no longer designed to be a mobile phone *app*, but rather a mobile phone website. We had initially planned to develop Mavigator as an iOS and Android app available on both the App Store and the Google Play Store, and while developing for Android is easy, iOS is where we faced many issues. There is a major fee for having apps listed on the App Store which would be a major setback to our project as we do not have the funds to list it on the App Store off a non-profit project.

### Indoor Floor Plans

We had planned on obtaining indoor floor plans from UTA directly via email request, but the email Anthony sent to UTA was left unanswered. More attempts to get into contact with UTA officials may be necessary. In the meantime, a clever workaround was found. By configuring an AI agent (Claude Code \[24\]) to scrape the Internet Archive, we were able to find many old Emergency Exit PDF maps and piece them together to get a semi-clear picture of many building interiors. However, these maps are majorly outdated and can be out of date. This was already experienced during the mapping of ERB floor 6, where the data was out of date, and was unable to be completed.

### Outdoor Building Outlines

Originally, we traced our shapes over the UTA PDF map \[16\] to get a layout of all buildings. However, we quickly realized that this would take many hours to get all 100+ buildings on UTA, as well as trace walking paths for every single building. In this iteration, we pulled data from Open Street Map and converted their nodes to the system that our map uses. However, Open Street Map’s data is not fully perfect so we opted for a combined approach where we place Open Street Map’s data on top of the Campus Digitizer tool \[23\] created in the previous iteration and re-traced certain buildings and defined new walkways. This system is far from perfect and will need significant work in future iterations.

### Continuous Integration

This iteration saw the usage of GitHub Actions \[11\] to automate deployment to GitHub Pages \[11\], allowing us to push our code and not have to worry about updating it on the web end. This itself came with many issues discussed later in this document including the pre-rendered pages causing a crash.

## Development Plan

Aside from the aforementioned changes in this iteration, everything went smoothly. The iterative development plan \[22\] we created last time still serves its purpose and is being closely followed. The only main concern is the amount of time allocation necessary to fully map building interiors. The first ever building mapped was Nedderman Hall, and doing so took 14 hours from one person. This was largely due to it being the first one, to which the Engineering Research Building only took 7 hours to finish mapping, and while both of these buildings are relatively large, these times to map a building’s interior is completely unrealistic for all 100+ buildings UTA has. To combat this, we have developed a tool for our developers called the Indoor Digitizer \[23\]. Its main purpose is to provide tools that allow us developers to map the interior of buildings significantly faster.

## Requirements Prioritization (MoSCoW)

Our inception phase did not prioritize any of our requirements, so it is now done. Doing the Musts first reduces the technical risks early. If the graph or the indoor model had failed, there was still time to change our approach before Iteration 3\.

| Priority | Requirement | Why | Risk it reduces |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Must | Outdoor campus graph and Dijkstra routing | Every route and the parking recommendation depend on it | R-07, R-09 |
| Must | Indoor room routing (NH first) | Top interview pain point, our only feature no competitor has | R-08 |
| Must | Schedule with a valid building link | A class is the destination of every route | R-04 |
| Should | Permit parking recommendation with walking ETA | Commuter interviews (Tan, Andy) | None new |
| Should | Residence and apartment start points | Resident interview (Blaine) | None new |
| Could | Settings allow units, 12/24 hour, saved data | Comfort, not core navigation | None |
| Could | MyMav import, foot traffic rerouting, lot fullness | Convenience, requested by only one user | R-05 |
| Won’t | Gather information on most crowded times | Requires real time student tracking and privacy reasons | None new |

## Competitor Uniqueness

Five tools already help UTA students get around. Each covers one piece of the trip, and none connects a student’s schedule and permit to the room they need.

| Feature / Capability | Google Maps \[26\] | UTA Static PDF  \[16\] | Modii (PATS Portal) \[27\] | UTA Interactive Map \[28\] | Maze Map \[29\] | Mavigator |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Outdoor Pedestrian Paths | Yes | No | No | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Permit-Filtered Parking | No | No | Partial | No | No | Yes |
| Personal Schedule Integration | No | No | No | No | Some | Yes |
| Indoor Room Navigation | No | No | No | No | Partial | Yes |
| Offline / Client-Only Execution | No | Yes | No | No | No | Yes |

**How Mavigator differs:** One trip, start to finish. It is the only tool that takes a student from their schedule to an allowed lot or their home, to the building’s best door, to the room. Room-level navigation at UTA today. None of UTA’s own tools route to a room. MazeMap could, but UTA does not license it. Free with no install or account. It runs in the phone’s browser, and settings stay on the phone. Where competitors are still ahead: Modii shows live lot occupancy, which UTA does not publish for us. Google Maps covers everything off campus; and only two buildings are mapped indoors so far.

# Risk Evaluation

Three risks were retired by completed work, R-08's exposure fell from 12.0 to 4.0, and two new risks appeared. Only risks tied to Iteration 2 work are listed. R-01, R-02 and R-05 are unchanged from inception. Updated probabilities and impacts are the team's proposed values.

## Retired Risks

| Risk | Was | Outcome |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| R-09: Hand-traced map drifts from real campus | 3.2 | Retired. Measured the old trace at 865 ft median error. Replaced it with OpenStreetMap data \[12\], georeferenced to 3.5 m median error |
| R-07: Need to switch map API | 1.5 | Closed. Realized in Iteration 1\. the app now has no map API dependency or API key |
| R-03: Cross-platform issues | 2.1 | Realized, then resolved. App Store release needs \$99/yr and a Mac build, so the product ships as a mobile website. Native builds still compile |

## Risks

| ID | Risk | Category | Probability | Impact | Exposure | Change |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| R-08 | No indoor plans for remaining buildings | External data | 20% | 20 | 4.0 | Down from 12.0. NH and ERB traced |
| R-04 | Some rooms or floors cannot be mapped | External data | 70% | 3 | 2.1 | Realized for ERB floor 6 and handled |
| R-10 (new) | Floor plan source is copyrighted (UTA EHS evacuation diagrams \[15\]) | Legal | 20% | 10 | 2.0 | New |
| R-11 (new) | Web pre-rendering breaks pages that read the clock or storage | Technical | 30% | 4 | 1.2 | New |
| R-01 | Remodel or demolition of a building | External Data | 50% | 2 | 1.0 | Down from 4.0. New tool usage |

## Risk Mitigation Plans

* R-08: As discussed earlier, UTA Emergency Exit PDF routes were scraped off the Internet Archive and used to map the interior of buildings. Though they are still outdated so a follow up email to UTA officials is necessary to obtain the most up to date maps. Aside from requesting these, our team can manually go into buildings and sketch out the layout of the building. Will follow-up email to UTA by 10/18. Woolf Hall traced in Iteration 2.5.  
* R-04: Emergency Exit routes cover every building’s interior, the only problem is whether or not they are outdated, as described in our previous risk mitigation strategy, this one will follow a similar structure. The mapping of ERB floor 6 has also shown that we can mark a floor as unmapped if necessary. Will recheck ERB floor 6 on site during Iteration 2.5.  
* R-10: The Emergency Exit PDFs themselves are copyrighted, but tracing over them is not. We still need to confirm with UTA officials if mapping indoors of buildings is allowed, and if not, we may need to add a UTA sign in to our app so that only UTA students can access it. Will ask UTA for permission by 10/18.  
* R-11: React expects the phone’s first run to make the same page as the build did, and anything that is different between them and the build time breaks. Our code can differ in the clock, saved data, and the windows themselves. To mitigate this, we use a function that makes the page show the build time version and then switches to real time and saved data once React takes over. Will check on every merge to main.  
* R-01: This risk has already been relatively mitigated but can never be fully eliminated. We now have a tool that allows for the tracing of buildings very quickly, and only having to map one building is significantly faster than mapping hundreds of buildings. Will re-check mapped buildings each iteration.

# Design

All data is generated at build time and all routing runs on the phone, so the app needs no server. This section follows a simplified IEEE 1016 \[20\].

## Architecture

![Architecture · build-time pipeline and run-time components][image1]

The figure above shows build-time pipeline and run-time components. The import turns map sources (OpenStreetMap \[12\] via the Overpass API \[13\], the PATS parking map \[14\], UTA Emergency Exit evacuation diagrams \[15\]) and hand edits into generated TypeScript data. On the phone, screens read shared state and ask the routing engine for routes.

Every input the user or the phone gives the app, and what the app shows in return.

| :---- | :---- | :---- |

## Route Calculation

1. Every tab asks one hook, usePlaceRoute(target, from), for a route. The target is a building, optionally with a room. Schedule, Map and Parking all use it.  
2. The hook resolves the start point (GPS, building, lot, pin or room) to a coordinate or node.  
3. findRoute snaps the start to the walkway graph and ends at the building's nearest entrance by path, or at the room's door node when the room is traced. If it cannot find an entrance (a building’s interior is not mapped) it routes from/to the center of a building.  
4. shortestPath (Dijkstra \[17\] with a binary min heap) runs once over the combined outdoor and indoor graph. We had an issue where the app would route through rooms, so edges through a room cost an extra 1,000 m, so routes use hallways and cut through a room only when no hallway leads there. Reported distances use real meters.  
5. splitRoute cuts the route where it enters the building. An outdoor part (walk or bike ETA) and an indoor part (walking, stairs counted).  
6. routeDirections simplifies each part (Douglas-Peucker \[18\] at 5 m) and writes steps: "Head west", "Take the stairs up to floor 3", "Room 340 is on your right".

Parking uses one shortestPathTree from the class building instead of one search per lot.

## Pages and Features

#### **Map tab**

* Shows the whole campus: buildings colored by category, parking lots, streets.  
* Tap **Legend** to see what the colors mean.  
* Tap a building to open its preview (name, category, abbreviation).  
* For a traced building (NH, ERB), switch the preview from **Outside** to **Inside**: change floors and tap a room.  
* Tap **Set as destination** (building) or **Set Room x as destination** (room) to open its route.  
* Long-press the map to drop a pin as your location. **Clear** removes it.

![][image10]![][image11]

Future fixes:

* One-finger panning in the indoor preview does not work until a pinch zoom starts.  
* The building preview takes too much space. Collapse it unless the user wants it.

#### **Route screen (from Map or Schedule)**

* Shows the walk from the start point to the building's best entrance, with distance and ETA.  
* Tap **From x** to choose a start: your location (GPS \[7\]), a residence hall, an apartment, a parking lot or a dropped pin.  
* Tap **Walk / Bike** to switch modes. Only the outdoor time changes because biking indoors is unlikely.  
* Open the drawer for turn-by-turn directions.  
* The start lights up green and the destination is marked with a red pin.  
* For a room, tap **Go inside** for indoor navigation.

#### **Indoor route screen**

* Shows the building's floor plan with the walk to the room, floor by floor.  
* Steps name the stairs or elevator and the side the room is on ("Room 228 is on your left").  
* Tap a step, or use the floor picker, to see that floor.

![][image12]![][image13]

#### **Schedule tab**

* Shows the user's classes for one day. The Su to Sa row opens on the current day of the week.  
* On today's list: a green check when done, "In progress" with a green glow, the next class with a yellow glow.  
* Tap **\+ Add class**: class name, class code, building (a searchable list), room number, days of the week, start and end time (native time picker \[6\]).  
* Tap a class to view its route.  
* Tap **Edit** to select and delete classes.

![][image14]![][image15]

Future fixes:

* Start and end time buttons go off screen on iOS.  
* Edit should let the user change a class, not only delete it.  
* Show the Add class button only outside Edit mode.  
* Center the day-of-the-week buttons.

#### **Parking tab**

* Choose a parking pass from the pass chip (nine student permits, Faculty/Staff, or None).  
* Lots are colored for that pass: green allowed, red not allowed, yellow opens at 1 PM. Lots with no rule stay gray.  
* The drawer recommends the three best lots for the next class today, ranked by walking time, with RECOMMENDED on the best one.  
* Tap a lot to draw the walk from it to the class.

Future fixes:

* Merge parking tab into Map tab in favor of having separate Navigation tab  
* Fix parking rules for different permits being inaccurate

#### **Settings tab**

* **Your Profile:** schedule editor (add or remove classes) and Parking Permit.  
* **App Customization:** Theme (System, Light, Dark), Time Standard (12 or 24-hour), Measurement Units (Imperial or Metric). Each applies across the whole app and is saved.  
* **About:** OpenStreetMap \[12\] credit.  
* **Developer (temporary):** simulated clock, test class in NH, start inside NH. Will remove before the final demo.

## Handled Exceptional Cases

* Room not traced. The route ends at the building's nearest entrance.  
* Floor not mapped (ERB floor 6). The indoor map shows a notice instead of an empty floor.  
* Start point inside the building. The outdoor screen is skipped.  
* GPS denied or unavailable. The start sheet says so and a dropped pin works instead.  
* No start point or no route for Set as destination. A message says what is missing.  
* Lot with no permit rule. Drawn gray, never shown as "not allowed".  
* No permit, no class left today, or building not on the map. The parking drawer says what is missing.  
* Add Class. Rejects no days selected and an end time at or before the start. Asks before adding a class that overlaps another or a room not on the building's indoor map.  
* Missing or corrupt saved data. Ignored, and the default value is used.

# Code

179 files changed since Iteration 1 (62,606 lines added, 4,181 removed). While this may seem like an absurd amount (it is), most added lines are generated map and indoor data from our Campus Digitizer and Indoor Digitizer tools meaning a majority of this is JSON files of building outlines and layouts.

| Module | Path | Purpose |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| OSM import | tools/osm/ | Rebuilds src/data/ from OpenStreetMap \[12, 13\] plus hand edits (map-edits.json, indoor-edits.json) |
| Indoor builder | tools/indoor/ | Turns indoor-edits.json into indoor nodes, edges and floor plans. Joins hallways that cross |
| Georeference | tools/digitizer/ | Fits PATS map \[14\] positions to lat/lng from 39 street landmarks |
| Routing engine | src/routing/ | geo, graph, dijkstra, route, legs, directions, eta, rooms, floors, start-point, parking-recommendation, format |
| One route system | src/hooks/use-place-route.ts, src/components/routing/ | usePlaceRoute plus the shared outdoor and indoor route screens used by every tab |
| Indoor map | src/components/map (IndoorMapView, FloorPicker) | Draws a floor’s rooms, stairs and route with react-native-svg \[4\]. Pinch 1x to 6x with Gesture Handler and Reanimated \[5\]. |
| Set as destination | src/app/map, poi-info-sheet.tsx | Building destination from the Map tab |
| Saved settings | src/state/persist.ts, src/app/\_layout.tsx, schedule-context.tsx | Saves and restores state in localStorage after the page loads |
| Units and time format | src/state/distance-unit.ts, time-format.ts, settings screens | Imperial/Metric and 12/24-hour applied app-wide |
| Parking drawer | src/components/parking | Top three lots, RECOMMENDED, legend |
| Web tab bar | src/components/app-tabs.web.tsx | Icon color on tab change. Full-resolution icons |
| Developer screen (temporary) | src/app/settings/developer.tsx | Simulated clock, test class in NH, start inside NH. Removed before the final demo |
| Web shell and deploy | src/app/+html.tsx, .github/workflows/deploy-web.yml, public/ | Mobile web page shell, Home Screen icon. Build and publish on every push to main |

## Notable Code

* Dijkstra with a binary min-heap. The graph has 2464 outdoor nodes plus the indoor nodes. An array scan would be quadratic and too slow to re-run on a render. Both ends accept several node ids, so a route leaves from or arrives at whichever door is nearest.  
* Junction-only graph. Only walkway junctions are nodes. The shape between them rides on the edge. This keeps the graph near 520 KB instead of 1.4 MB.  
* Entrance routing. Routes end at the building's nearest entrance by path, not its center. Nedderman from the north: 149 m to the north door instead of 249 m around the building.  
* Room penalty. Edges through a room cost 1000 extra meters in the search only, so routes stay in hallways unless a room is the only way in. Distances shown to the user are real.  
* Indoor directions. Consecutive stair flights merge into one step, and the side of the hallway a room is on comes from the angle of its door spur.  
* Georeference. A moving least-squares fit gives each point its own affine transform weighted to nearby landmarks. One affine was not enough: the PATS drawing \[14\] is shifted 20 to 30 m near the west edge.  
* Hydration guard. The web build is pre-rendered at build time. Anything that reads the clock, storage or window, including saved settings, waits for useHasHydrated(), or React discards the page.

## Unit Tests

All 506 Jest \[9\] tests in 36 files pass, up from 151 tests in 12 files at Iteration 1\. All of these tests were written by AI (Claude \[24\]) asked to obtain significant coverage over the file they were testing. TypeScript \[8\] type check and lint report 0 problems. Test documentation follows a simplified ISO/IEC/IEEE 29119-3 \[21\].

# How To Test / Run

If you want to simply see the website itself, it is now hosted at [antovu.github.io/cse3311-fall26-group7](https://antovu.github.io/cse3311-fall26-group7/map), though we may choose to move away from GitHub Pages at a certain point for a better URL. As for running the code itself:

`git clone https://github.com/AntoVu/cse3311-fall26-group7.git`  
`cd cse3311-fall26-group7`  
`npm install`  
`npx expo start --web --tunnel`  
`npm test      #in a different terminal if tunnel still running`

Please note: this project is designed as a website now, but is still made specifically to be used on the phone. Future iterations may improve the looks and functionality on desktop, but for now, desktop testing should not be a priority. The site was also checked at phone size in an emulated touch browser using Playwright \[10\]. Navigate to the link provided by the tunnel to test on your phone.
